change.description: feat(workflow_engine): Add in hook for producing occurrences from the stateful detector
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: The class now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`. The base class leaves `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` abstract (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:142-170). `Detector.detector_handler` calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86). For any detector of type `metric_alert_fire`, that call now raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. Before this change it returned a handler whose `evaluate` returned `[]`. `process_detectors` has no guard around the call, so one such detector aborts processing for the whole packet and for the remaining detectors. Either implement the abstract methods, or keep the handler as a plain `DetectorHandler` returning `{}` until the stateful version is built.

findings.title: Stale TODO comment
findings.body: The comment says "This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction", but the class is now a `StatefulDetectorHandler` subclass. The comment should be updated or removed.

findings.title: Expected occurrences are built with a value that differs from the evaluated value
findings.body: `test_results_on_change` and `test_dedupe` evaluate `val1` with 100 and 8, but build the expected occurrence with value 6. The mock builder ignores `value`, so the tests pass. They would not catch a bug where the wrong value is passed to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. The same applies to `test_state_results_multi_group`, where the second group has value 10 but the expected occurrence uses 6. Use the real values, and make the mock encode the value in the occurrence (for example in `evidence_data`).

contracts.action: Detector.detector_handler instantiates MetricAlertDetectorHandler, which is now a StatefulDetectorHandler
contracts.equivalent_path: Other grouptypes' handlers, such as the test MockDetectorStateHandler, implement every abstract method.
contracts.before_after: Before: a concrete handler whose evaluate returned []. After: the class is abstract because no abstract methods are implemented, so instantiation raises TypeError.
contracts.visible_effect: process_detectors raises for any detector of type metric_alert_fire.
contracts.failure_mode: TypeError propagates out of process_detectors with no handling, so the other detectors in the packet are not processed.

summary: The main problem is that `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` becomes an abstract `StatefulDetectorHandler` subclass with no implemented methods. Detectors of type `metric_alert_fire` would then raise `TypeError` when `Detector.detector_handler` instantiates the handler. The rest of the refactor (dict results, `build_occurrence_and_event_data` hook) is consistent. The tests use expected values that don't match the evaluated ones, which weakens them.
